title: Collections Platform Reference: Three-Payment Settlement Offers on Own Authority
content:
# Three-Payment Settlement — Extending the Offer

The Three-Payment Settlement is a programme of Ridgeline's Settlement Agreements under which a consumer settles one placed account in three settlement payments.

## Scope and standing terms

This rule prices a Three-Payment Settlement offer that Ridgeline extends on its own authority on a placed account whose placing agreement is a Starter Contingency Agreement or a Standard Contingency Agreement, the two agreement tiers whose client-tier floor reduction is 0.0; an offer on an account placed under any other agreement tier, or on an account whose same-client accounts include one with a balance due under 300.00 dollars or one that cannot take a settlement, is outside this rule and stays under the base rules.

Ridgeline extends the Three-Payment offer on its own authority at exactly the Three-Payment offer percentage, never at another percentage.

A Three-Payment offer is never a Hardship Settlement, so no hardship hold is needed to extend it.

## When the percentage is fixed

The Three-Payment offer percentage is fixed only after every other open account of the consumer under the same client agreement whose balance due is under 500.00 dollars carries an open Two-Payment offer dated the offer date.

Put the other way: so long as any such account under that agreement shows no open Two-Payment offer dated the offer date, the Three-Payment offer percentage is not yet fixed.

## What the platform action does

`issue_three_payment_settlement_offer_bcdb6a79` extends a written Three-Payment Settlement offer on one placed account on Ridgeline's own authority. One call opens a new settlement for the account in status offered, dated today, under the Three-Payment Settlement programme: three settlement payments 30 calendar days apart, the first falling due 15 calendar days after today if the consumer accepted today, and the offer open for acceptance through the 30th calendar day after today. The offer records the balance, percentage and amount given, carries no client approval, and books nothing to the settlement balance until it is accepted. The consumer and the agent can see the new offer, with its reference, expiry date and due dates, among the account's settlements.

## How it is invoked

An agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `issue_three_payment_settlement_offer_bcdb6a79`, then calls it.

## Parameters

- `account_id` — identifier: the Ridgeline account reference number of the placed account the offer would settle, as returned by the placed-account lookup for the verified consumer.
- `balance_at_offer` — USD to 2 decimal places: the account's balance due today, exactly as the placed-account lookup shows it; no rounding beyond the cent.
- `settlement_pct` — percent to 1 decimal place: the settlement percentage offered (62.5 means 62.5 percent of the balance).
- `settlement_amount` — USD to 2 decimal places: the amount that settles the account in full; the tool stores it as given, rounded only to the cent.
- `bundle_applied` — enum, `true` or `false`: `true` when the offer is extended as part of a bundle covering the consumer's accounts under one client agreement and the bundle reduction is in its percentage; `false` when the offer stands alone without any bundle reduction.

## Return

A text rendering of a dictionary with `settlement_id` (the new settlement reference), `status` (always "offered" on success), `variant_name` ("Three-Payment Settlement"), `offer_date` and `offer_expiry_date` (YYYY-MM-DD), `settlement_pct` (percent, 1 decimal), `settlement_amount` (USD, 2 decimals), `payment_count` (integer 3), `first_payment_due_date` and `final_payment_due_date` (YYYY-MM-DD, assuming acceptance today) and `bundle_applied` (true or false). A returned `settlement_id` means the offer was recorded.
